description: The sanctioned-divergence registry for the Stage 133 cross-implementation differential suite (tools/hls-xdiff.py). The suite's oracle is cross-backend agreement; every divergence it finds is a FINDING, and this ledger is where a finding becomes an owned fact instead of a swept-away failure. Every entry names ONE program (file basename), the backend that owns the divergence (culprit), the per-backend state signature that was observed when the divergence was diagnosed, and a diagnosis that says what is actually wrong. The ledger is two-way, like Stage 128's: a divergence whose entry is present with a matching signature is SANCTIONED (the run stays green and quotes the diagnosis back); a ledgered program that now compares clean is STALE (the entry must be trimmed — the divergence was fixed, which is good news the ledger must not outlive); a ledgered program whose observed states no longer match the entry is a MISMATCH (the divergence moved or grew — re-diagnose, never auto-pass); and a divergence with no entry is the REGRESSION alarm this suite exists to wire. Draft new entries with `python3 tools/hls-xdiff.py --update-ledger`, classify and diagnose them by hand, and splice them in — the tool never writes this file. Entries were built from the Stage 133 first sweep (v0.151.0-alpha) over the full gated corpus; the two soundness entries are the loudest: the wasm alpha does not emit the runtime refinement guard, and does not bounds-check byte_at — the interpreter panics 101 where wasm runs on and prints output the other backends never print.

waivers.diagnosis: str.to_float() is not implemented in the wasm alpha: hl_str_to_float is emitted as a bare `unreachable` (tools/hlwasm_parts/hwasm_emit_runtime.py, _emit_hl_str_to_float — 'for the alpha, raise a clean error'). The program halts at its first to_float() call; the interpreter and the native build run it clean to exit 0. The suite keeps this visible until the parse path is implemented.

The wasm emitter produces a module Node refuses to compile: 'Compiling function #26 failed: call[0] expected type i32, found i64.const of type i64'. The monomorphized generic call path emits an i64 constant where the callee signature says i32 — a typing bug in the emitter's generic lowering, hit by nested generic instantiation. The interpreter and the native build run the program clean; wasm cannot even load it.

The wasm emitter's tail-call lowering loses the return value on the stack: Node rejects the module with 'expected 1 elements on the stack for return, found 0'. The same source runs clean on the interpreter and compiles and runs clean natively, so the suite holds the wasm emitter's tail path to the table until its stack discipline is fixed.

A value divergence, not a representation drift: the fixture computes d = 9.223372036854776e18 (INT64_MAX as a double, 2^63) and branches on d > 1e17. The interpreter and the native build take the branch; the wasm backend does not (its output ends three lines early, exit 0, no trap). The printed value of d canonicalizes to the same double on every backend, so the divergence is in the f64 comparison path (or the literal bits feeding it) for doubles at or above 2^63 — a wrong answer, exactly the class this table exists to keep loud.

SOUNDNESS. A refinement violation at runtime must be a clean panic (exit 101) in BOTH implementations — the fixture's own comment says the 'unreachable' println must never run. The interpreter and the native build panic 101 on the guard; the wasm backend does not emit the runtime refinement guard at all, prints the unreachable line, and exits 0. A missing check, not a formatting drift — the loudest finding of the first sweep.

SOUNDNESS. s.byte_at(7) on a three-byte string must panic with 'string access out of bounds' (exit 101). The interpreter and the native build do; the wasm backend returns 0 for the out-of-bounds byte and exits 0 — the bounds check is not emitted on the wasm byte_at path. A silent out-of-bounds read shaped as a value is exactly the class of divergence this suite must keep loud.
